messages:
mike: Heads up — saw a regression on multi-GPU runs after landing the CUDA-graph replay change. Large tail latencies and throughput drop when KV-cache warmup is enabled. Timeline: https://redwood.internal/perf/2133334444 :thinking_face:

anya: Ugh. Is this the job that uses tensor+pipeline parallel? Any specific model or seq len where it spikes?

mike: yeah tensor+pipeline, seq = 2048 mostly. Affected on p4d and nvidia A100 clusters. Not all runs, seems tied to replay + KV warmup sequence.

sofia: Can you paste a short perf trace? nvtx/nsight timeline would help, but even a small nvprof stack is useful.

mike: attaching excerpt from Nsight timeline (trimmed):
```
- kernel: fwd_chunk_1 (stream 200)
- cudaGraphReplay begin -> captures launch on stream 200
- allreduce start (stream 201) waits on event from stream 200
- subsequent kernel launched on stream 202 blocked on allreduce
- host sync observed between replay and first allreduce (micro-pauses ~300-800us)
```

ben: That pattern screams stream-affinity mismatch + event ordering during graph replay. If replay rebinds streams or reuses them differently, the recorded event dependencies can get lost causing implicit host-syncs.

anya: Could KV-cache warmup be racing with the rolling allreduce window? We do a bunch of prefetches that touch KV cache on separate streams. If those prefetches are recorded in the graph differently vs runtime path, replay might serialize.

mike: Exactly my speculation. When we enable KV warmup (prefetch of past KV segments) the timeline shows extra memcopies on a different stream immediately before replay. After replay starts, allreduce appears to be forced to wait for completion.

perf-bot: Perf regression alert: multi-gpu throughput -18% (p95 latency +42%) on job redwood/inference/bert-large (2133334444). Related PR: r/infra/7063.

sofia: Repro steps for local-ish run? We need something small that still reproduces the overlap failure.

ben: Quick repro idea: run 2-GPU pipeline toy with seq=1024, set REDWOOD_CUDA_GRAPH=1, enable KV_PREFETCH=1, and use the batch heuristic that triggers per-sample padding. Command: 
```
REDWOOD_CUDA_GRAPH=1 REDWOOD_KV_PREFETCH=1 REDWOOD_BATCH_MODE=dynamic python -m rdinfer.repro --model small-tp --gpus 2 --seq 1024 --iters 200
```
Should be quick and show a throughput drop if you profile.

anya: Also try with CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=0 and then with =1 to see where host-side barriers are introduced. If switching to =1 makes it disappear, that's a clue it's host sync induced by event waits.

mike: I ran the repro. With graphs+kv-prefetch we see interleaved host_sync markers in nvtx. Without kv-prefetch it's clean.

sofia: Two plausible root causes: 1) our graph capture routine is reassigning stream indices at capture time so events recorded outside the graph get treated as host-synced; 2) kernel selection fallback path (we switch to a fallback kernel when quantized path not available) inserts small cudaDeviceSynchronize() in error path. Both would break overlap.

ben: On point 2 — we added a fallback in kernel selector for small seq lengths that does a quick sanity sync. It was supposed to be only local, but if that path runs during replay it becomes global and serializes allreduce. Check kernel_selector logs for "fallback-sync" entries.

mike: Found logs: 
```
[2026-03-15T09:12:37Z] kernel_selector: chosen=quant_fwd_128, fallback-sync=true, reason=tile_mismatch
```
So fallback-sync flips on under certain tile combos.

anya: Ok, immediate mitigation options: 1) disable fallback-sync during replay (unsafe but quick); 2) ensure KV prefetches are also recorded into the graph or scheduled on same stream affinity so replay doesn't reorder them; 3) change batch heuristic to avoid the tile_mismatch that triggers fallback.

sofia: For a longer-term fix we should: (a) make graph capture preserve external event dependencies by inserting user events into the graph; (b) remove any implicit device syncs in kernel fallback path and instead return an error code that forces higher-level retry outside replay; (c) add a unit test that runs graphs+kv-prefetch under multi-gpu to catch regression.

ben: I can prototype (b) quickly — replace cudaDeviceSynchronize() with a per-stream event-based wait and bubbles up the sync indicator. That should avoid global sync during replay.

mike: I'll prepare a small timeline clip and attach to the ticket. Also will flip off KV_PREFETCH by default in the replay config until we ship a fix.

anya: Who's owning the follow-up? We need a small PR with kernel-selector change + test and an infra tweak to ensure capture includes prefetch streams.

sofia: I can take the capture side (ensure we either record those streams or inject events). Ben takes kernel-selector patch. Mike will handle config toggle and perf regression ticket.

mike: Thanks — setting a quick sync point: PRs by EOD Friday, tests green before merge. If anyone hits a blocker ping me or @sofia. :thumbsup:

ben: I'll start a draft branch now and link it.

perf-bot: Deploy canary started for infra/7063 with KV_PREFETCH=0. Canary ID: c-2133334599.

mike: Good. Keep notes in the ticket (infra/7063) and we can close this thread once we verify canary fix.

anya: One more note — add a perf metric in console that correlates allreduce idle time with graph-replay usage so this doesn't surprise us later.

sofia: Agreed. I'll add a dashboard tile.

mike: Closing loop — thanks all.
